title: The Sextet at the Friedrichsbau: a Paris child, five broadcasting systems, and a record that outran her
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Paris, birth into the family trade
stops.date_confidence: attested; both Wikipedia editions agree on the day. The coordinate is the canonical central-Paris pin the atlas already uses for Coco Chanel's house at 31 rue Cambon, standing in because no source names an arrondissement, a street, or a clinic.
stops.campa: On the fourteenth of January a daughter is born in Paris to Giuseppe Valente, an accordionist, and Maria Valente, called Siri, a musical clown. The family has been in show business for generations and she is born into the trade the way other children are born into a farm. Her father's people come from a hill town in Lazio; her mother's craft is the circus ring and the timed fall. No document records the room; only the city itself, Paris, is fixed, and the record says so plainly.
suggested_refs: Registers of Paris births, January 1931, not located in this research pass

stops.name: San Biagio Saracinisco, the father's hill town
stops.date_confidence: no event at this place carries a date in any source. The stop repeats the birth date so the segment runs forward; Giuseppe Valente's own dates, 1891-1957, are given by German Wikipedia, and the year he left the village is not recorded anywhere consulted. The first-pass coordinate was about 9.5 km northwest, in the wrong valley.
stops.campa: Above the Comino valley in the province of Frosinone stands the village Giuseppe Valente leaves. A few hundred souls, stone and terraces, the kind of place a musician quits with an accordion on his back and does not come back to. Il Messaggero remembers it on the day his daughter dies ninety-three years later, in a headline saying that the father was from San Biagio. She will sing in more languages than any two sources can agree on. One of them will be his, and Italian television will build two series on it.
suggested_refs: Il Messaggero, 11 September 2024, 'Morta Caterina Valente, il padre era di San Biagio'

stops.name: Stuttgart, the sextet at the Friedrichsbau
stops.date_confidence: year attested by both editions; no month recorded. Coordinate warning: the historic Friedrichsbau of 1898 stood near the Oberer Schlossgarten, roughly 500 m north of this pin, and the coordinate German Wikipedia now attaches to the name belongs to a different house opened on the Pragsattel in December 2014.
stops.campa: At five she plays guitar in the family sextet at the Friedrichsbau, and a working life begins that will not end for sixty-seven years. Her siblings are on the same bill; the German account puts her very first stage in a circus ring. The house she plays in burns out entirely in the raid of the night of 25 July 1944 and is pulled down in 1955 to widen a street, so nothing at the address survives to be visited. Neither edition of her life records what the sextet played. Both record that it was paid.
suggested_refs: Photographs of the original Friedrichsbau, Stuttgart, 1898-1944

stops.name: Breslau, the year the accounts divide
stops.date_confidence: year only, and the two Wikipedia editions describe incompatible events at this place. Neither gives a month. The pin is the city centre because no source names a street, a shelter, or a camp.
stops.campa: The family tours occupied Europe playing to German troops, and at Breslau the record splits in two. The English account has a thirteen-year-old surviving the bombing and helping to pull people out of it. The German account has the family imprisoned here and then deported east. Neither confirms the other and neither is dropped. Within three years the city will be Wroclaw and in another country. The girl who leaves it will spend her working life singing in the language of the army her family played for.
suggested_refs: The Allied bombing of Breslau and the 1945 siege, contemporary photographs

stops.name: The Soviet Union, an internment with no address
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction throughout. German Wikipedia says deportation to the Soviet Union, English Wikipedia says Russian camps, and neither gives a camp, a city, a month, or a route home. Both the coordinate and the month are declared placeholders and carry no evidential weight.
stops.campa: German Wikipedia says deportation to the Soviet Union. English Wikipedia says Russian camps. Between them they name no camp, no city, no date of arrival, and no road by which a family of Italian variety performers got back to France. The pin is Moscow because a coordinate is required here and the sources supply none more specific. This is the largest hole in the whole life: a year or more of it, at thirteen or fourteen, surviving only as a direction of travel and a word for what was done to them.
suggested_refs: Records of Italian nationals deported eastward from Silesia, 1944-1945, not located

stops.name: Paris, the nightclubs and Gilbert Becaud
stops.date_confidence: year attested by German Wikipedia; no month. The pin is the canonical central-Paris coordinate again, because no source names a single club.
stops.campa: At sixteen she is back on the coordinate she was born on, singing chansons in Paris clubs for whatever a room pays. Some of the songs are written for her by Gilbert Becaud, who is nobody yet. Both editions carry him; neither carries the name of one club. A tour through Scandinavia follows, which is how a Paris nightclub singer comes to make her first records in Copenhagen. She stands on Chanel's pin seven years before Chanel returns from Switzerland and reopens the house on it.
suggested_refs: Gilbert Becaud's earliest songwriting, before his own performing career

stops.name: Copenhagen, the first records
stops.date_confidence: year attested by German Wikipedia only; no month, and the English edition does not mention the session at all.
stops.campa: A seventeen-year-old sings into a microphone with a quartet behind her, and a career that will run to more than thirteen hundred recordings begins in a Danish studio. German Wikipedia carries the session and the English edition does not mention it. No label is named, no studio, no titles, no personnel beyond the word quartet. What survives is a city and a year and the Scandinavian tour that put her there. The beginning of one of the largest discographies in Europe is otherwise gone.
suggested_refs: Danish recording-industry registers for 1948, not consulted in this pass

stops.name: Zurich, the Circus Grock and Walo Linder
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no month, and no studio address is given, so the pin is a city coordinate. The marriage date is disputed: English Wikipedia gives 1951, German Wikipedia 1952. Both agree the marriage ends in 1971, so only the start year is in question.
stops.campa: Walo Linder, head of entertainment at Radio Zurich, hears her sing at the Circus Grock and brings her into the station, where her first record is cut and passed on to other broadcasters. The same year she marries Gerd Scholz, a German juggler working as Erik van Aro, who becomes her manager. An earlier draft of this account had the clown Grock personally urging her toward singing; the German text says only that Linder heard her at his circus. The circus is the venue, not the mentor, and the distinction is kept here.
suggested_refs: Radio Zurich entertainment department under Walo Linder, early 1950s

stops.name: Baden-Baden, the audition for Kurt Edelhagen
stops.date_confidence: year attested by both German articles; no month. Place corrected: English Wikipedia puts this audition at Suddeutscher Rundfunk in Stuttgart, about 68 km east, but Edelhagen directed the Sudwestfunk orchestra at Baden-Baden from 1 January 1952 to 31 March 1957 and never held a post at Stuttgart.
stops.campa: She sings for an hour in several languages for the director of the Sudwestfunk dance orchestra, and he says the thing that will be quoted for the next seventy years. English Wikipedia moves this audition to Stuttgart and the wrong broadcaster; the German article on Edelhagen settles it, because he held Baden-Baden from the first of January 1952 to the last of March 1957 and nothing at Stuttgart ever. In April 1957 he leaves for the WDR in Cologne. By then her first record is made, and it has failed.
stops.quote: Das ist die musikalischste Frau, die ich je gehört habe!
stops.quote_source: Kurt Edelhagen after the 1953 audition, in direct speech as given by SWR4, 'Caterina Valente: ein Weltstar mit vielen Talenten', 11 September 2024. English Wikipedia renders the same remark as indirect speech, which the first pass mistook for a quotation.
suggested_refs: The Sudwestfunk Tanzorchester under Kurt Edelhagen, Baden-Baden, 1952-1957

stops.name: Cologne, Istanbul fails and O Mama does not
stops.date_confidence: the 29 March 1954 recording date is attested by English Wikipedia. The place is not: no source names a recording city for either title. The pin is the atlas's canonical Cologne coordinate, chosen because the producer Kurt Feltz and the composer Heinz Gietz worked from Cologne, and it is a reconstruction rather than a record.
stops.campa: The first single is a jazz number called Istanbul, cut for Brunswick with Edelhagen, Gietz and Feltz behind it, and it sells nothing at all. Feltz tells her that Schlager is her form. She records O Mama, O Mama, O Mamajo and it is a hit immediately. The turn takes a few months and decides everything after it: the jazz singer the festivals will keep claiming becomes the Schlager singer German radio cannot get off the air. Nobody wrote down which studio either record was made in.
suggested_refs: Brunswick Records German releases, 1954; the working studios of Kurt Feltz and Heinz Gietz in Cologne

stops.name: Cologne, Ganz Paris traumt von der Liebe
stops.date_confidence: release year 1954 per the German discography, correcting a first-pass 1955; no month recorded. The recording city is unattested and this pin is the same declared Cologne reconstruction used for the Istanbul session. A first-pass figure of 500,000 copies in the first year appears in neither edition and has been dropped.
stops.campa: Cole Porter's I Love Paris, sung in German, becomes the record that fixes her. Polydor will not see another like it: over nine hundred thousand copies, the house sales record, and by Der Spiegel's flat accounting in January 1959 still short of the million that would have made it legendary. She is twenty-three, singing about the city she was born in, in the language of the country her family toured for during the war, on a record made in a studio that no source has ever named.
stops.quote: Die Valente zählte unbestritten zu den Spitzenstars des Polydor-Repertoires, obgleich bislang kein Valente-Titel die legendäre Auflage von einer Million überschreiten konnte – den Verkaufsrekord hält die Nummer Ganz Paris träumt von der Liebe mit einer Auflage von über 900.000 Platten.
stops.quote_source: Der Spiegel, 'Good bye, Caterina', Nr. 3/1959, 13 January 1959. A journalistic assessment of her, not her own words.
suggested_refs: Polydor single 'Ganz Paris traumt von der Liebe', 1954

stops.name: Berlin, Malaguena and The Breeze and I
stops.date_confidence: Malaguena is dated 1954 and The Breeze and I 1955 by the German discography; the first pass had conflated the two into one 1955 session. Berlin is a reconstruction from Werner Muller's broadcasting base and is attested by no source at all.
stops.campa: She records with the Werner Muller orchestra and one of the sides crosses the Atlantic. The Breeze and I spends fourteen weeks on the American charts and passes a million copies by 1978. It is the record that makes her a name outside German-speaking Europe, and it does so without a word of German in it. Neither Wikipedia edition says where either session happened. Muller worked out of Berlin, so the sessions are placed in Berlin here, and the guess is marked as a guess.
suggested_refs: The Werner Muller dance orchestra, Berlin, mid-1950s

stops.name: Hollywood, The Colgate Comedy Hour
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no broadcast date given. The venue is a reconstruction: the series ran production units in New York, Chicago and Los Angeles, and no source ties her appearance to the Sunset and Vine studios. The first-pass coordinate was also about 0.4 km north of that intersection.
stops.campa: Her first American television appearance, alongside Gordon MacRae, four years after she was singing in Paris cellars for what the room paid. The Colgate Comedy Hour is a national institution and she arrives on it as a European curiosity who can sing in whichever language the sponsor prefers. Nine years later she will be co-hosting a CBS series of her own. Which coast this broadcast came from cannot be said here: the show worked out of three cities and nobody recorded hers.
suggested_refs: The Colgate Comedy Hour, NBC, 1955 season with Gordon MacRae

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the Second German Jazz Festival
stops.date_confidence: year attested by German Wikipedia; no month, and the hall within Frankfurt is not named, so the pin is a city coordinate.
stops.campa: A major success at the second German Jazz Festival, in the same year the Schlager records are selling by the hundred thousand. From here the two careers run side by side and never merge: the hit parade takes the German songs, the festivals and the American musicians take the voice. She is claimed by both and settles into neither. The German press calls her a Schlager star in the same months Chet Baker books her for a session. The hall she sang in is not recorded.
suggested_refs: The Deutsches Jazzfestival, Frankfurt, second edition, 1955

stops.name: Munich, the sessions with Chet Baker
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no month, and no source names a city, so the Munich pin is a declared placeholder rather than a location. The first pass wrongly bundled two albums into this session; The Hi-Fi Nightingale is 1956 and Plenty Valente! is 1957, and the Baker work is two singles.
stops.campa: Two sides with Chet Baker: I'll Remember April and Ev'ry Time We Say Goodbye. Not an album, which the first reading of this life got wrong, and not a novelty either. The trumpeter is in the middle of his European years and she is the German record industry's largest seller, and the two of them cut a pair of standards together. German Wikipedia lists the titles and the year and stops. The city is missing here, as it is missing for almost every record she made in the fifties.
suggested_refs: Chet Baker's European sessions, 1956

stops.name: German television, Bonsoir Kathrin
stops.date_confidence: start year attested by both editions; the run continues to 1964 and the two disagree on the episode count, one giving ten. No production city is named by either, and the Frankfurt pin stands in for the ARD without support.
stops.campa: The first German personality show, built around her, running to 1964 with Peter Alexander beside her. The pairing becomes the standard German television duet of the decade: he charming, she able to do whatever the sheet in front of her asks, in whatever language it is written in. The show is the reason a West German generation knows her face and not only her records. Where it was made is not established here. The sources give a title and a span of years and no address whatever.
suggested_refs: Bonsoir, Kathrin!, ARD, 1957-1964, with Peter Alexander

stops.name: Oberflockenbach, the villa in the Odenwald
stops.date_confidence: occupancy 1957 to 1962 is attested by German Wikipedia; no month. The first-pass coordinate was about 2.2 km off, and this one is the village given by the German article. The exact villa address is not published.
stops.campa: A villa is built for her in a village above Weinheim and she lives in it with Gerd Scholz until 1962. A son is born during those years. It is the only fixed address of her German career that any source records, and it does not stay hers: a later owner, Curt Engelhorn, gives the property to the University of Heidelberg as a seminar house. The Odenwald is an hour from Frankfurt and a world away from the Friedrichsbau, where the sextet was paid out of what came through the door.
suggested_refs: The Valente villa at Oberflockenbach, later a seminar house of the University of Heidelberg

stops.name: Munich, Hier bin ich hier bleib ich, with Bill Haley
stops.date_confidence: English Wikipedia dates the filming to 1958, the German filmography the release to 1959; no month for either. No studio or city is named and Munich is a placeholder for West German film production.
stops.campa: She films a picture with a guest appearance by Bill Haley and His Comets, and sings a duet with him on a re-recorded Vive la Rock and Roll. Rock and roll is two years into Germany and the industry's answer is to put it inside a Valente vehicle. She is twenty-seven and has by now sung jazz with Chet Baker, Schlager for Polydor, chansons in Paris cellars and rock and roll with the man who started it. The film is shot in 1958 and reaches the cinemas in 1959.
suggested_refs: Hier bin ich, hier bleib ich (1959), with Bill Haley and His Comets

stops.name: Hamburg, the contract that leaves Polydor
stops.date_confidence: Der Spiegel reports the announcement as coming the same day as the split with Polydor, but the parenthetical 29 December 1958 that circulates with the passage is a Wikipedia editor's gloss and does not appear in the article. The date is carried as the best available reading, not as attested. Hamburg is Teldec's seat and is a reconstruction.
stops.campa: The Grammophon-Gesellschaft sees its largest seller off with a headline, Good bye Caterina, and the same day her secretary announces that she has already signed with Teldec after strictly secret negotiations over the Christmas days: the most significant record contract offered to a German singing star since 1945. Der Spiegel prints the whole manoeuvre in January with the sales figures attached. She is twenty-seven, and the record industry of a country she was not born in is bidding against itself for her.
stops.quote: Noch am gleichen Tage verlautbarte der Sekretär der Sängerin, Günter Arendt, die Valente habe »nach streng geheimen Verhandlungen in den Weihnachtstagen« bereits mit der »Teldec Telefunken-Decca Schallplatten GmbH« den »bedeutendsten Schallplattenvertrag« geschlossen, »der einem deutschen Gesangsstar nach 1945 angeboten wurde«.
stops.quote_source: Der Spiegel, 'Good bye, Caterina', Nr. 3/1959, 13 January 1959. The guillemets are the magazine's own; this is her secretary Gunter Arendt's press statement, not her speech.
suggested_refs: Teldec Telefunken-Decca Schallplatten GmbH contract announcement, December 1958

stops.name: Beverly Hills, the second Grammy Awards
stops.date_confidence: the ceremony date is attested. Whether she attended, and at which of the two simultaneous ceremony cities, is unrecorded, so the coordinate is a reconstruction. The first pass placed this at the first Grammy Awards of 4 May 1959, which honoured 1958 recordings and did not include her.
stops.campa: La strada dell'amore is nominated for best female vocal performance. The category that year reads Ella Fitzgerald, Lena Horne, Caterina Valente, Pat Suzuki, Peggy Lee. Fitzgerald wins. The nomination is the American industry's formal notice of a singer whose home market is German radio, and it falls in the same twelve months as Bongo Cha Cha Cha, a record that will outlive everything else on this list by sixty years. No source says whether she was in either room.
suggested_refs: 2nd Annual Grammy Awards, 29 November 1959, Best Vocal Performance Female

stops.name: Rome, the Italian seasons at Via Teulada
stops.date_confidence: years attested for both series, six episodes in 1961 and nine in 1962; no months. The Via Teulada production centre opened on 19 December 1957 and is the standard Rai television site of the period, but no source names it for these programmes, so the building is a reconstruction.
stops.campa: Rai builds two series around her, Bonsoir Catherine in six parts and then Nata per la musica in nine. Her father's language, her third or fourth working one depending on which count is believed, gets a television career of its own alongside the German and the American ones. She is running three national broadcasting systems at once, in three languages, with a fourth waiting in Paris. German Wikipedia gives the episode counts. It does not say where in Rome she stood to make them.
suggested_refs: Rai production centre, Via Teulada 66, Rome, opened 19 December 1957
sources: Wikipedia, 'Centro di produzione Rai di Roma' (Italian edition)

stops.name: New York, eight nights with Perry Como
stops.date_confidence: the run of eight appearances is attested for 1961 through 1966; no individual broadcast date is given. The pin is a Broadway-district placeholder because the show's origin city varied across its run and no source specifies hers.
stops.campa: Eight appearances between 1961 and 1966, the longest recurring American engagement of her career. Como's hour is a settled fixture of American television and she is the guest who can be handed anything: a bossa nova, a German number, a duet in whatever key. The Broadway billing and the Las Vegas debut get a line apiece in the record. These eight hours are what the American decade is actually made of, a foreign singer turning into an ordinary face in American living rooms.
suggested_refs: The Perry Como Show, NBC, guest appearances 1961-1966

stops.name: New York, CBS Studio 50 and Ed Sullivan
stops.date_confidence: three appearances are attested; no broadcast date is given for any of them, so this year is a placeholder inside the American decade and is not attested. Name warning: the building was CBS Studio 50 throughout her run and was renamed the Ed Sullivan Theater only on 10 December 1967.
stops.campa: Three times through the doors at 1697 Broadway, on the programme that decides what America has heard of. The building is not called the Ed Sullivan Theater yet and will not be until the end of 1967; through her entire run it is CBS Studio 50. The sources that record the three appearances record nothing else about them: no dates, no songs, no billing, no order. It is the most famous stage she stood on in the United States, and what she did on it cannot be said.
suggested_refs: CBS Studio 50, 1697 Broadway, renamed the Ed Sullivan Theater on 10 December 1967

stops.name: New York, CBS Studio 50 and The Entertainers
stops.date_confidence: premiere date attested, 25 September 1964, with the series running 26 episodes to 27 March 1965. The first pass gave 22 episodes, a figure carried only by the Valente article, and placed production at CBS Television City in Los Angeles, which is the wrong coast.
stops.campa: Twenty-six episodes of a CBS variety series, co-hosted with Carol Burnett and, at the start, Bob Newhart. In January the show moves from Friday at half past eight to Saturday at nine, Newhart and several regulars leave, and Burnett and Valente carry the remainder between them. The following year she takes the FAME award as best female vocalist on American television from the hands of Sammy Davis Jr. The series is made in the same building on Broadway that Sullivan broadcasts from.
suggested_refs: The Entertainers, CBS, 25 September 1964 to 27 March 1965, from CBS Studio 50

stops.name: Las Vegas, the first Strip engagement
stops.date_confidence: year attested; no month, and neither a hotel nor a showroom is named by any source consulted. The pin marks the central Strip and is a placeholder.
stops.campa: She plays Las Vegas for the first time, and in the same year headlines a Broadway show of her own. Neither the hotel nor the theatre is named anywhere reachable: not the run, not the notices, not a single song. The two engagements that mark the summit of her American standing survive as one sentence apiece in an encyclopedia. The German series that made her famous at home is documented down to the episode count. The American peak is a rumour with a year attached to it.
suggested_refs: Las Vegas Strip showroom bookings, 1964; the unnamed Broadway engagement of the same year

stops.name: London, the session for The Caterina Valente Singers
stops.date_confidence: the album is dated 1964; no month. The Jimmy Page claim is sourced only to the trivia page of the artist's own website, with no corroboration from any session log on the guitarist's side, and both the claim and the London location are reconstructions.
stops.campa: An album called The Caterina Valente Singers, on which, the story goes, a young session guitarist named Jimmy Page is among the players. The only source is the trivia page of her own website. No discography from his side, no session log, nothing independent whatever. It is the sort of detail that circulates because it is pleasing, and it is recorded here as pleasing and unsupported. London is where such session work was done, and that is the only reason the pin sits there.
suggested_refs: The Caterina Valente Singers (1964); London session work of Jimmy Page, 1963-1966

stops.name: Mainz, the ZDF and AVRO seasons
stops.date_confidence: the run is 1966 to 1968 in eight episodes, a ZDF and AVRO co-production; the first pass compressed it into a single 1966 season. No production site is named and the Mainz pin stands in for the ZDF as a reconstruction.
stops.campa: Die Caterina Valente-Show, eight episodes across three years, made jointly by German and Dutch television. The Goldene Kamera comes the same year. She now has, or has had, a series of her own on German, Italian, Dutch and American networks, and will add Austrian in 1982. What she does not have is a country: born French, Italian by parentage, resident in Switzerland, employed by Germany. No production site is named for any of the eight episodes. The audience on the other side of the screen is the same one every time.
suggested_refs: Die Caterina Valente-Show, ZDF and AVRO, 1966-1968

stops.name: Bonn, the Federal Cross of Merit
stops.date_confidence: year attested by both editions; no month, and no presentation site or presenting officer is named. The Bonn pin stands in for the federal capital and is a reconstruction.
stops.campa: The Order of Merit of the Federal Republic, First Class, and by both accounts the first show-business star to receive it, though neither edition sources that claim. The Republic decorates a woman born in Paris whose family spent the war playing to its army and whose German is a working language rather than a mother tongue. Eighteen years later it will give her the Great Cross of the same order. Neither edition says where this one was handed over, or by whom.
suggested_refs: Bundesverdienstkreuz Erster Klasse, 1968

stops.name: London Palladium, the Royal Variety Performance
stops.date_confidence: year attested and the programme is sourced to Radio Times of 15 November 1970; the day of the performance itself is not given in the material consulted. The first-pass coordinate was about 0.4 km off, near Golden Square.
stops.campa: She sings Before the Parade Passes By and The Breeze and I at the Royal Variety Performance, on the stage British variety treats as its cathedral. The second of those songs is fifteen years old by now and still working. Radio Times prints the programme on the fifteenth of November. Through these same years she is a regular at the Talk of the Town in the old Hippodrome on Cranbourn Street, and not one of those engagements is dated anywhere in either edition.
suggested_refs: Royal Variety Performance 1970, London Palladium, Radio Times 15 November 1970

stops.name: Olympia, Paris, seven returns
stops.date_confidence: the seven Olympia engagements are attested by German Wikipedia and not one of them is dated. This year is a placeholder inside her touring decades and carries no evidential weight.
stops.campa: Seven times on the boulevard des Capucines, in the hall that is to French song what the Palladium is to British variety. She was born a mile and a half from this stage and sang in the clubs around it for a living at sixteen. The house that takes her back seven times is the house Becaud made his own, the writer who handed a teenage unknown her first songs. German Wikipedia counts the seven engagements and dates none of them, and no French source reached in this research supplies the years.
suggested_refs: Olympia, 28 boulevard des Capucines, Paris, engagement registers

stops.name: London, the marriage to Roy Budd
stops.date_confidence: year attested by German Wikipedia and corroborated by Roy Budd's own article; no month, and no source on either side names a location, so the London pin is inferred from Budd's career base and is a reconstruction. The 1974 son is a German-edition detail that the English sources do not carry at all.
stops.campa: One year after the divorce from Gerd Scholz she marries Roy Budd, British composer, arranger and jazz pianist, who had written the score for Get Carter two years before and works mainly out of London. A second son follows in 1974, a detail the German edition carries and the English one does not mention. They divorce in 1979. Where the wedding took place is recorded on neither side, and neither gives a month. The London pin is inferred from Budd's working base.
suggested_refs: Roy Budd's compositions and film scores of the early 1970s

stops.name: Moscow, a tour with no itinerary
stops.date_confidence: German Wikipedia states that she performed in the USSR without naming a city, a venue, or a year. Both the coordinate and the date are declared placeholders. The pin repeats the one the atlas used for the 1944 deportation, for the same reason: no source will name a place.
stops.campa: She sings in the Soviet Union at some point in the Cold War decades, and that is the entirety of the record. The same is true of Japan, of Australia, of South Africa: German Wikipedia lists the countries and stops there. A performer whose whole claim is that she worked in every language on the continent has almost no attested itinerary outside Europe and the United States. The record returns her to the same Moscow coordinate used for the wartime deportation, thirty years on, because the sources still refuse an address.
suggested_refs: Soviet concert-agency records for Western performers, 1960s-1970s, not consulted

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the South American circuit
stops.date_confidence: South America appears in German Wikipedia's list of tour destinations with no city, venue, or year. The Buenos Aires coordinate is the atlas's canonical South American pin used as a declared placeholder, and the date carries no evidential weight whatever.
stops.campa: South America is on the list of places she worked, and nothing else about it is on any list at all. Forty-five years later the record that outlives everything else, Bongo Cha Cha Cha from 1959, will begin its second life in Latin American accounts on a telephone application before spreading back to Italy and Germany. The continent that goes unrecorded in her touring history is the one that hands her back to the world. Buenos Aires is a placeholder for a whole continent with no dates on it.
suggested_refs: Latin American tour itineraries of European variety artists, 1960s-1970s, not located
sources: QUEUE.md and the atlas's canonical Buenos Aires pin

stops.name: German television, Manuel and the end of the second marriage
stops.date_confidence: the hit and the ZDF-Hitparade appearances are dated 1978 without a month; the divorce from Roy Budd is dated 1979. The Mainz pin stands in for the ZDF and is not attested for any particular broadcast.
stops.campa: Manuel is a hit and she is back on the ZDF-Hitparade with it, twenty-four years after Ganz Paris and in a market that has changed underneath her twice over. Rock and roll came and went, and the hit parade is still running her. The following year the marriage to Roy Budd ends. She is forty-eight, has been working since she was five, and has another twenty-five years of stage life in front of her, which is longer than a good part of the audience watching her sing has been alive.
suggested_refs: ZDF-Hitparade appearances with 'Manuel', 1978

stops.name: German television, Wunsche die ich mir erfulle
stops.date_confidence: year attested by English Wikipedia alone; no broadcaster, no run length, no production city, and the German edition does not list the programme at all. The Frankfurt pin is the same declared ARD placeholder used for Bonsoir Kathrin.
stops.campa: She begins hosting a show whose title means the wishes I grant myself. It is the fourth format built around her name across four decades of German television, and the only source that mentions it gives a year and nothing else: not the network, not the run, not the number of episodes. The German edition, which lists her television work down to the co-producing broadcaster, does not carry it. The two encyclopedias are not describing the same career here.
suggested_refs: Wunsche, die ich mir erfulle, West German television, from 1981

stops.name: Vienna, the ORF at the Kuniglberg
stops.date_confidence: the series runs across 1982 and 1983 in eight episodes; no month is given. The ORF-Zentrum Kuniglberg is the standard production site and is not explicitly named in the source; the first-pass coordinate was about 4.5 km off, in the wrong district of the city.
stops.campa: Caterina, eight episodes for Austrian television across two years, out of the broadcasting centre on the hill southwest of Schonbrunn. Austria is the fifth national television system to give her a series with her own name on it. She is fifty-one. The first stage was a Stuttgart variety house in 1936 and the sextet took what came through the door; the ledger since then reads Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, the United States and now Austria, and not one of those countries is hers.
suggested_refs: Caterina, ORF, 8 episodes, 1982-1983

stops.name: Mainz, second place in a viewer vote
stops.date_confidence: the ZDF-Hitparade broadcast of 26 May 1984 is the cited source for the placing. The Mainz pin stands in for the ZDF and is not attested for this broadcast.
stops.campa: Manner brauchen Liebe takes second place on the ZDF-Hitparade and she is handed a trophy for it, a Golden 2. The German body text calls this second place in Germany; the awards list underneath the same article corrects it to second place in a television programme's viewer vote, decided by the people watching at home. A chart position and a viewer vote are not the same thing, and the second is what is carried here. She is fifty-three and still on the show that sold her records in 1959.
suggested_refs: ZDF-Hitparade broadcast of 26 May 1984 and the Goldene 2 trophy

stops.name: Sindelfingen, fifty years on the stage
stops.date_confidence: the jubilee, the ARD special, the Guinness entry and the Great Cross all fall in 1986; no month is recorded for the presentation, which Lothar Spath made at Sindelfingen near Stuttgart on the occasion of the fifty-year stage jubilee.
stops.campa: Fifty years since the sextet at the Friedrichsbau, twenty miles up the road from this hall. Lothar Spath hands her the Great Cross of the Order of Merit. ARD broadcasts Bravo, Catrin! and nearly seventeen million people watch it. The Guinness Book enters her as the most successful female recording artist in Europe with more than thirteen hundred and fifty recordings, not albums, and the evidence for the entry is a photograph of the certificate on her own website.
suggested_refs: Bravo, Catrin!, ARD, 1986; the Guinness certificate photographed on caterinavalente.com

stops.name: Cologne, the Kurt Weill concerts
stops.date_confidence: year attested by German Wikipedia; no month. The Philharmonie and the WDR Big Band are both named by the source, so this is one of the few precisely located performances in the whole file.
stops.campa: Jazz concerts with the WDR Big Band and the Cologne Philharmonic, issued on disc only years afterward as Kurt Weill: American Songs. The year before she had made A briglia sciolta, an Italian jazz record reissued as Fantastica and again as Platinum Deluxe, which becomes the best-selling compact disc of her career worldwide. At sixty she is working in the city Edelhagen left Baden-Baden for in 1957, and in which Salomon Oppenheim's house once discounted the bills of the whole Rhine.
suggested_refs: Kurt Weill: American Songs, WDR Big Band, recorded Cologne 1990

stops.name: Bissone, Girltalk and the end of the working life
stops.date_confidence: the album is dated 2000, the Echo lifetime award 2002, and the end of performing 2003; no month for any of the three. No source attaches a place to the retirement, and the first pass invented one. The pin is the Bissone residence the German edition gives for her later decades.
stops.campa: Girltalk, a duet record with the harpist Catherine Michel, is the last studio album. The Echo for lifetime achievement comes in 2002 and in 2003 she stops performing. She has been on a stage since 1936. The first reading of this life placed the retirement at Bissone; no source does, and the place is struck. What the sources do give is a village on the Lugano lake where she lived for decades, and a Californian second home she later sold, saying it was because of the Trump administration.
suggested_refs: Girltalk (2000), with the harpist Catherine Michel

stops.name: Munich, the last public appearance
stops.date_confidence: attested: the 57th Bambi gala at Munich on 1 December 2005. German Wikipedia calls it her last appearance before a mass audience, which is stronger than the first pass allowed.
stops.campa: The honorary Bambi for lifetime achievement, at the fifty-seventh gala. German Wikipedia says plainly that this is her last appearance before a mass audience, not merely one of the last. She is seventy-four. The shelf behind her by now carries a Goldene Kamera, a Bambi and a Bambi for a lifetime, a Goldene Europa, an Ehren-Prix Walo, a Platinum Romy, an Echo, and two grades of the Federal Cross of Merit. After this evening the public record of her goes quiet for nineteen years.
suggested_refs: 57th Bambi gala, Munich, 1 December 2005, Ehren-Bambi

stops.name: Bissone, the withdrawn decades
stops.date_confidence: no year can be fixed for the withdrawal. German Wikipedia describes her later life as very retired and records interviews in 2009 and 2019; this date is a placeholder standing for a period, not an event, and is not attested.
stops.campa: She lives, the German edition says, sehr zuruckgezogen, very withdrawn, keeping contact with the public through a Facebook page of photographs and memories rather than through appearances. The interviews amount to almost nothing: one in 2009, one in 2019 that the outlet publishing it describes as her first in thirteen years. In that one, at eighty-eight, from the village on the Swiss lake, she gives the whole account of herself in a single sentence and does not enlarge it.
stops.quote: Ich habe alles gemacht, was ich machen wollte, einiges besser, anderes schlechter – wie jeder, glaube ich.
stops.quote_source: Caterina Valente, interview published on her Facebook page, quoted in Schlager Planet, 'Happy Birthday, Caterina Valente', 14 January 2019. Fetched directly and confirmed.
suggested_refs: The Caterina Valente Facebook page of personal photographs and memories

stops.name: Hollywood, Bongo Cha Cha Cha comes back
stops.date_confidence: the film's 2019 release year is attested and no month is carried in the material consulted; the TikTok trend is dated 2021 by the same source. The pin repeats her 1955 American television placeholder, because the two events belong to the same industry and neither has a recorded address.
stops.campa: A 1959 side goes into the soundtrack of Spider-Man: Far from Home, and two years later the same three minutes carry a trend past two hundred and fifty million views on TikTok, beginning in Latin American accounts and spreading from there to Italy and Germany. She is eighty-eight and then ninety, in a house on a Swiss lake, while a record she made at twenty-eight outruns the entire rest of the discography. Neither edition of her life says whether anybody asked her about it.
suggested_refs: Spider-Man: Far from Home (2019) soundtrack; the 2021 TikTok trend on 'Bongo Cha Cha Cha'

stops.name: Lugano, death in the house on the lake
stops.date_confidence: attested by both editions: 9 September 2024, at her home in Lugano, aged 93. The exact address is not published, so the pin is a city coordinate.
stops.campa: She dies at ninety-three in her own house, on the lake she had lived beside since the years when German television was still building programmes around her name. Between the Friedrichsbau in 1936 and this room lie eighty-eight working years, more than thirteen hundred recordings, five national broadcasting systems, and a number of languages no two sources will agree on: six spoken and thirteen sung, or eleven sung, or the ten that journalism keeps repeating with no tally behind it.
stops.quote: Caterina Valente che io chiamo maestra è una musicista pazzesca, e come voce, come padronanza, rimane la più forte.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Mina, cited by Italian Wikipedia to tg.la7.it, 11 September 2024. The outlet itself was not reachable in this research and the attribution is unverified beyond that citation.
suggested_refs: Italian obituaries of 11 September 2024, including the Mina tribute

stops.name: Lugano, a testament and no grave
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. No date is recorded for the funeral, for the opening of the testament, or for any interment; this date is a placeholder immediately after the death and is not attested by anything.
stops.campa: A handwritten testament is opened by the Magistrate of Lugano, said to set out her wishes for the funeral and the memorial. Her former manager tells the German press that he learned of her death from the media, and Focus runs the word Eklat over it. Where she is buried is published nowhere reached in this research. No street carries her name, no square, no star on any pavement, no grave of honour, no museum room. The most recorded singer in Europe has no monument that any source consulted can locate.
suggested_refs: Focus, 'Eklat nach Beerdigung von Caterina Valente', 2024, body text not fetched
